name: Saint-Cyprien / Canet – Pont des Basses
notes: Signed kite area at the south end of the Canet Lido, by the Pont des Basses (a dedicated area is also signed on Saint-Cyprien north beach). Check the towns' summer rules. Waves with SE / thermal; tramontane offshore: experienced riders.

name: Le Barcarès – Les 3 Colonnes
notes: Official kite zone; narrow launch behind the dunes. Waves with marin (SE) and summer thermal; tramontane offshore. Also: Parc des Dosses on the Étang de Leucate for flat water by tramontane (experts).

country: # archived: the Leucate tourist office lists Le Goulet for windsurf / wingfoil / SUP only and puts the free kite zone at Coussoules; blogs disagree on a kite sector towards Île de la Rascasse

name: Leucate – Le Goulet
notes: Shallow flat water on the Étang de Leucate below Leucate village; first place the tramontane hits. Helmet and impact vest recommended (shallow).

name: Leucate – Les Coussoules / La Franqui
notes: Famous tramontane spot (Mondial du Vent); the tramontane (NW) is offshore here: experts only. Waves with marin (SE). In season the kite zone is the one secured by the KSL club beside the old lifeguard post (windsurf zone upwind, to the north). The exit channel on the La Franqui cliff side is closed to kites.

name: Étang de La Palme
notes: Shallow flat-water lagoon, safe by tramontane (onshore at the launch); schools on site. Good for learning.

name: Gruissan – La Vieille Nouvelle
notes: Glassy water by tramontane, which is offshore and strong: experienced riders, drift risk, no lifeguards. Sandy track access (2.15 m height bar). No riding on the Étang de l'Ayrolle. Also: Les Chalets 3 km north (waves with marin), Narbonne-Plage 8 km north-east.

name: Sète – Pont-Levis
notes: Étang de Thau reference flat-water spot, kite zone open all year. Launch from the sandbank safe zone, one kite at a time; no jumping in front of the launch or along the dyke. Tramontane (NW) onshore; avoid east wind (offshore, gusty off Mont Saint-Clair). Keep clear of the hospital heliport zone and, in summer, of the second dyke (nesting birds). Booties (urchins). Also: Marseillan and Mèze on the Étang de Thau; Les 3 Digues on the sea side (summer kite zone).

name: Carnon – Petit Travers
notes: The town's official kite zone, certified by the French sailing federation: 200 m of beach between access points 73 and 74, with a 50 m buffer each side; in summer a channel is used only to leave and rejoin the shore. Works with the S–SW thermal and the SE marin; tramontane and mistral are offshore here. Narrow rigging area shared with beachgoers, first 30 m of water very shallow, dune posts near the waterline: intermediate and up. Les Roquilles (Carnon west) is reported closed to kites in summer. Also: La Grande-Motte (Couchant and Grand Travers zones), Maguelone 12 km south-west.

name: Le Grau-du-Roi – L'Espiguette
notes: Huge wild beach of fine sand, the area's reference: works S, SE, SW (thermal, easiest) and NW (tramontane, side-shore). Schools take students over by boat from Grau-du-Roi town (about 15 min); by road it is a long walk from the car park. In summer the kite zone is split from the bathing area by a line of yellow buoys, and the beach is crowded with swimmers and boats. Also: Port-Camargue – Plage Sud (flat by NW / mistral) and Le Boucanet (W waves).

name: Beauduc
notes: Wild, remote beach on the Golfe de Beauduc: wide, shallow water, easy launch. Works in mistral (NW) and S, SW and W; only a straight E blows off the shore. Kite zone is marked on the beach apart from the swimmers, stay inside it. Access is an unpaved track of about 8 km through the salt pans, vehicle access is regulated and there is no driving on the beach. Protected site. Schools work from here, based in Salin-de-Giraud. Piémanson is about 20 km east.

name: Port-Saint-Louis – Plage Napoléon
notes: Long sand spit between the Rhône mouth and the Gulf of Fos, in a protected area, facing the open sea: SW, S and SE (SE brings the biggest waves and the Rhône current); mistral is strong and gusty. All levels, a kite school is based nearby (Mistral Kite Passion). Big car park, paid in summer. No official kite-zone text found. Carteau, the sheltered bay, is about 3 km north-west.

name: Marignane – Le Jaï
notes: 5 km sand strip between the Étang de Berre and the Bolmon lagoon, one of the windiest places in Provence (about 250 wind days a year): mistral (strong, gusty), SE and W thermal. Ride only on the Étang de Berre side, the Bolmon side is a nature reserve. Warm shallow water, good for learning; rocks along the beach. Schools and a kite club on site (Jawaï, kite13).

name: Carro
notes: Experts only. No real beach: a rocky shelf about 400 m wide, tight launch with a shore break, sea urchins (wear booties) and a strong current at the point. Best with SE (side-shore, waves); W and E also ride; the mistral is offshore and dangerous, N is flat. One local source says kiting is limited to the north side of the beach. Free parking at the harbour.

name: Marseille – Pointe Rouge
locate: q:Plage de la Pointe Rouge Marseille
notes: Marseille's classic mistral spot for advanced riders: NW (gusty) and W are best, S and SE make waves in front of the breakwaters, E can be boosted by the Marseilleveyre gap. Tight rocky launch from a narrow slab, little room, crowded in summer. October to May riders use the north of Bonneveine beach (La Bassine). Kiting is banned on the beaches in summer: the dates here (about 15 June to 15 September) are NOT confirmed by an official text, one blog quotes a prefectoral order of 2020 (300 m from the beach) that I could not find. Check before going.

name: Six-Fours – Le Brusc
notes: Plage des Charmettes, sheltered from swell by the Embiez islands; SW to NW (mistral). Technical launch (rocks). Kiting banned June–September.

name: Hyères – L'Almanarre
notes: World-famous W / SW spot. Kite zone between beach gates 16 and 21 with marked channel; ride beyond the 300 m buoys. Town rules (Hyères kite code): launch only from the marked channel, nothing in the 300 m band outside it, beach marshal 15 June–15 Sept. Crowded in summer. Also: Le Mérou (L'Ayguade) for east wind.

name: Fréjus – Saint-Aygulf
notes: Summer: kite zone at the Argens mouth (Base Nature side); late Sept to early June: Saint-Aygulf (Esclamandes) kite zone. Thermal S and E winds.

name: Bonifacio – Piantarella
notes: Shallow flat water behind the sandbank to Piana island; E / NE wind (avoid W). July–August: no room to rig, schools only.

name: Bonifacio – Tonnara
notes: World-renowned W (libeccio) spot in the Ventilègne gulf; flat by east wind. The closed bay of Pont de Ventilègne next door suits beginners. Also: Balistra (wild beach with lagoon, flat by W).

name: Figari – Baie de Figari
notes: Closed, shallow bay, very safe: ideal for beginners. Works with W (thermal, libeccio, mistral); E wind is gusty. Large kite school (Eole Figari). Four submerged rocks in the middle of the bay (buoyed in summer) and a busy narrow gulf with boats and jet-skis. One guide says the bay is closed to kites in summer and kiters launch about 15 min on foot to the south: no official text found, so check with the school.

name: Porto-Pollo – Plage du Taravo
notes: Summer thermal almost every afternoon; kite zone marked by yellow buoys (managed by an association). Launch on the right side of the beach near the campsite, at the Taravo river mouth. Good for beginners and foil. No lifeguard; the seabed drops off steeply, boats anchor close, rocks along the shore.

name: Calvi – La Pinède
notes: Big sandy bay; W (libeccio) and NE. Summer: head to the north-east end of the beach (Plage de la Légion side, 800 m walk from the Club Olympique), away from swimmers; one guide says kiting at the Club Olympique itself is tolerated only from mid-September. Gusty, breakwaters and a military zone at the east end.

name: Lac de Monteynard
notes: Famous alpine lake. Summer thermal from the north builds around 13:00 and holds until about 18:00 (8-12 kt); NE and NW are turbulent, south wind is gusty and irregular, often before storms. One small launch at the Onekite club beach (Treffort, paid parking); kite only in the marked zones, leash required, watch the ferry. Two schools, no lifeguard.

name: Narbonne-Plage – Créneau Naturel

notes: Kite banned by prefectoral decree (VNF). Formerly tolerated only in a small zone reached via the Auberge Le Cathare (Belflou). Venturi with autan (SE), often 25–30 kn+. Not for beginners; leave the water when firefighting planes operate.

name: Sérignan – La Grande Maïre
notes: Summer: kite only in the short zone between Sérignan-Plage and Portiragnes-Plage. Thermal / marin sea breeze.

name: Agde – La Tamarissière
notes: Agde's official kite zone, at the west end of the beach (gravel track); the only place in Agde for kiting in summer. Works W to SE; north wind is offshore and gusty. Groynes near the shore: not for beginners. Also: Richelieu Est in Cap d'Agde, 4 km east (by the jetty, schools ride from a boat).

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — Étang de Thau

name: Marseillan – Étang de Thau
notes: Western Étang de Thau at Maldormir, near Marseillan-Plage: flat shallow water, best in tramontane (N to NW, onshore). Small launch; don't walk inland (protected bird area). Keep clear of oyster farms. Also: the Marseillan village shore (Tabarka, Kithau school) 3 km north.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — Étang de Thau

name: Mèze – La Pinède
notes: North shore of the Étang de Thau by the Le Taurus nautical centre: flat water and waist-deep sandbanks, good for learning; backup when the sea is too rough. Southerly winds are onshore; tramontane (NW) blows off the shore. School on site (Fil d'Air).

name: Sète – Les 3 Digues
notes: Lido beach between Sète and Marseillan with a kite zone at beach accesses 53–54: one of the few beaches kited in summer. Southerly thermal onshore; avoid north wind (offshore, gusty). Watch for swimmers in summer.

Frontignan – Étang d'Ingril

name: Villeneuve-lès-Maguelone – Maguelone
notes: Summer: the only kite zone is on the Maguelone lido between the Prévost car park and the cathedral (the Prévost beach itself is reported closed to kites April to September; paid car park and little train in season). From June to September launch and return only through the signed channel (federation sheet). The KWM club secures the zone in July–August and at weekends in spring and autumn. Works SW and NW; tramontane is offshore: safety boat.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — continuation of Petit Travers / Grand Travers

name: La Grande-Motte
notes: Official kite zone beside the port (Couchant beach, west of the jetty): the town says a marked area is reserved for kites when the weather allows. Best with SE (side-shore, small waves against the jetty); S–SW also work; too much E is turbulent behind the port. In summer a channel along the jetty is only for leaving and rejoining the shore. Intermediate and up. Also: the town's second kite zone at the west end of the Grand Travers beach (access points 59–60), 1.6 km west, same winds; the 2014 town order (check it is still in force) activates both zones only with S / SE wind above force 5.

name: Lac du Salagou
notes: Kite tolerated (Natura 2000). Small grassy launch with trees, left of the road before the campsite: advanced riders. Tramontane stronger than on the coast.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 5 km from L'Espiguette

name: Le Grau-du-Roi – Le Boucanet
notes: Right-bank beach of Grau-du-Roi, the bay's wave spot: best with W and NW (tramontane brings waves along the beach), S–SW also work. Evening wind often turns N and drops behind the buildings along the beach. Guides say it is closed to kites from 1 June to 15 September, but their decree numbers disagree and no official page was found: check the town hall. Experienced riders.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 3 km from L'Espiguette

name: Port-Camargue – Plage Sud
notes: Sheltered behind the long jetties of Port-Camargue; best with NW (tramontane, flat water), W is onshore and N side-shore. Tough to get past the jetties, so experienced riders; schools also use it for lessons outside July–August. The usual fall-back when Le Boucanet is closed in summer.

country: # pro: Windy marks Saintes-Maries (wave and speed); restored from archived

name: Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer – Plage Est
notes: East of the Saintes-Maries harbour: the purpose-built speed canal gives flat mistral speed sessions, S and SE make waves; waves also break west of the harbour (E, SE, W). Paid access, kiting tolerated; no official kite-zone text found.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — Beauduc / Napoléon cluster

name: Salin-de-Giraud – Piémanson
notes: Long wild beach at the Rhône mouth, near Salin-de-Giraud (schools in the village): best S and SW. Strong currents near the Rhône mouth with SE wind; the bottom drops off fast. Since 2016 prefectoral measures stop wild camping and regulate vehicles on the beach, none about kiting. No kite ban found.

country: # pro: separate bay from Plage Napoléon (about 3 km)

name: Port-Saint-Louis – Carteau
notes: Closed bay of the Golfe de Fos, on the east side of the Port-Saint-Louis spit: flat water with S or SE wind, beginner to intermediate; Mistral Kite Passion school. Mistral is gusty; beware of drifting onto the mussel farms. Plage Olga (town beach on the same bay, 2 km north, industrial) is not a separate spot.

country: # pro: restricted (club / permit / summer ban) — banned in summer

name: Fos-sur-Mer – Le Cavaou
notes: Beach at the end of the road on the Gulf of Fos, facing S: SE, E and S work (SE / E for waves), summer SW thermal gives 10-15 kn; the mistral is offshore and gusty. Shallow, any level; keep clear of windsurfers. Signs say kiting is forbidden but show no dates and riders mostly come out of season: the 15 June to 15 September ban is a worst-case guess, no official text found. Industrial skyline and tankers.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — second Hyères zone

name: Hyères – Le Mérou
notes: Hyères' second official kite zone (L'Ayguade), for east wind: flat by west wind, choppy by east wind. Small launch area: intermediate / advanced.

name: Cannes – Palm Beach
notes: Only kite spot of Cannes (Pointe de la Croisette, old heliport launch). Very narrow rocky launch, boat traffic: experienced riders only.

name: Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer – Les Lecques
notes: Kite spot of the Baie des Lecques, used outside the bathing season only: the Saint-Cyr tourist office lists it open 16 October to 14 March, launching from the south end of the beach (beach 3 car park, near the Tapis de Sable hotel) and riding beyond the 300 m line. No wind or level information found: check the town hall before going.

name: Bormes-les-Mimosas – Cabasson
notes: Small bay beside the Fort de Brégançon, listed by the regional tourism board as a kite and windsurf spot, open 1 October to 31 May only. The beach faces south-west, so the mistral (NW) blows side-shore, which fits the tourism listing (mistral days"); one guide also names E / NE / SE for the Brégançon side. Intermediate and expert riders."

name: Bonifacio – Balistra
notes: Wild beach with a shallow lagoon behind it. Flat water by W (offshore, venturi), small waves by E. The local school closed in 2023.

name: Lac de Serre-Ponçon – Boscodon / Crots
notes: Only kite spot of the lake: Plage des Eaux Douces at Crots, with the Altitude Kite school (May-September). Thermal wind builds late morning and afternoon, gusts can arrive suddenly. Lake rules (police regulation, June 2020) apply: keep out of bathing areas and ask the school about the zone.

name: Lac du Bourget – Aix-les-Bains
notes: Kite club zone at Aix-les-Bains: ride fast and jump only beyond the yellow buoys (200 m). 'La Traverse' W thermal, late afternoon; erratic: advanced riders.

name: Leucate – Les Pilotis (Leucate Plage)
notes: Sea beach at Leucate Plage, between Leucate and Port-Leucate; kitesurf and kitefoil listed by the Leucate tourist office. Waves with marin (SE), a bit bigger than the nearby beaches; tramontane offshore: experienced riders. Check the town's summer beach rules.

name: Argelès-sur-Mer – Plage Nord
notes: North end of the Argelès beach. Shorebreak (steep beach). Waves with marin (SE) and summer thermal; tramontane offshore. Only a spot guide lists it as a recent kite spot and no school is on site: check the town's summer bathing rules before launching.

name: Algajola – Plage d'Algajola
notes: Sandy beach with shallow water (300-500 m); works NE, W and NW, also S. Intermediate level, experts enjoy it too. Surfers ride the west part of the bay; mind other beach users in July and August and currents when the swell is big.

name: L'Île-Rousse – Plage Napoléon
notes: Spot guide: SW wind (libeccio) for freeride and raceboard; N to NE winds give some waves. Town beach: crowded in summer, check the town's bathing rules.

name: Saint-Florent – La Roya
notes: Large sheltered gulf open to N and NW winds, protected from the libeccio by the Balagne mountains; shallow area at La Roya for intermediate riders. Check bathing and mooring zones in summer.

name: Lozari
notes: Long sandy beach, constant wind but gustier than at Algajola, mostly chop with small waves. One spot guide says kiting is not allowed in summer: no official text found, so check with the town before riding in July and August.

name: Pinarellu
notes: Bay near Porto-Vecchio with a sailing school offering kitesurf and windsurf (Ecole de Voile de Pinarello). Spot guide: a rare N wind makes it very good. Busy in summer: check the beach rules.

name: Ajaccio – Capo di Feno
notes: Surf beach (Grand Capo) exposed to W and SW; one article says it also works for kite, with ENE as the best wind. Waves and shorebreak: experienced riders. Surf club on the beach.

Sète – La Corniche
notes: Sand beach at the start of the Corniche, sheltered by a big breakwater, with a water-sports area on the right-hand side marked by a line of buoys. Flat water in north-west wind (side-shore to offshore, gusty near the dyke); east to south-east winds bring a small shore-break. Lifeguarded in summer: keep out of the bathing area.

region: Marseillan village shore of the Étang de Thau

name: Marseillan – Village (Kithau)
notes: Marseillan village shore of the Étang de Thau, at the Tabarka leisure park where the Kithau school has been based since 2003. Shallow lagoon water facing east: easterly and south-easterly winds are onshore, tramontane (NW) blows off the shore. Next to the port and oyster farms: keep clear. Another launch, Maldormir, is 3 km south.

name: Frontignan – Les Aresquiers
notes: Sea beach at the east end of Frontignan-Plage, listed as a kite spot with a kite zone at its Frontignan end. Small launch with the road close and gusty wind at the edge: for experienced riders. Tramontane (NW) blows off the land. Keep clear of swimmers in summer; check the town's beach rules before riding.
